questions.subject: english
questions.question_text: The expression,... stress is an issue every body can relate to experientially, means that .
questions.instruction: comprehension passage IIThe expression,... stress is an issue every body can relate to experientially, means that .
questions.passage: Stress is by far the common cause of ill health in our society and may be the underlying cause of as many 70-80 percent of all visits to family doctors it is also the problem that every doctor shares with patients. Expert notes that stress is an issue everyone can relate to experimentally in studying and better understanding about stress we can derive personal as well as professional benefitsStress can be overcome without undergoing duress. They often say any one who wants to help someone deal with his or her stress should learn to handle his / hers first. The manifestation of stress are legion. It can contribute or mimic just about any symptoms you can think of. However the main symptoms are physical, mental, emotional and behavioral thinking. The causes of stress are multiple and varied but they can be classified into external and internal. External stressors can include relatively getting sick or dying, jobs being lost or people criticizing or one becoming angry. However most of the stress people experience is self –generated. Experts tell us that we create the majority of our upsets indicating that because we cause most of our own stress, we can do something about it, this gives us measures of choice and control that we do not always have when outside forces act on us. This also leads to basic premise about stress reduction, to master stress change you have to figure out what you are doing that is contributing to your problem and change it. These changes fall into behaviour, thinking, lifestyle choices and /or situations you are getting to the root causes of your stress you can prevent recurrences. As a way of draining off stress energy nothing beats aerobic exercise. To understand why we need to review what stress is. People often think of stress as pressure at work, a demanding boss, a sick child or rush hour traffic. These may be triggers but stress is actually the body reaction to factors such as these. Stress is the fight or flight response in the rate of body, mediated by adrenaline and other stress hormones and comprised such physiological changes as increased heart rate and blood pressure, faster breathing, muscles tension, dilated pupils, dry mouth and increased blood sugar. In other words stress is the state of increased arousal necessary for an organism to defend itself at a time of danger. Exercise is the most logical way to dissipate the excess energy. It is what our bodies are trying to do when we pace around or tap our legs and fingers. It is much better to channel it into a more complete exercise like a brisk walk a run a bike ride or a game of squash.Just as we are all capable of mounting up and sustaining a stress reaction, we have also the ability to put our bodies into a state of deep relaxation called the relaxation response in this state all the physiologic event in the stress reaction are reversed. Pulse slows blood pressure falls, breathing slows and muscles relax Adapted from VANGUARD, 19th march 2008

options.option_a: it is better understood when experienced
options.option_b: its problem can be solved by.everybody

questions.explanation: The phrase 'relate to experientially' means that the subject (stress) is something people have personal, lived experience with. In the context of the passage, stress is described as a common cause of ill health that every doctor and patient shares. Therefore, 'everybody encounters it' is the most accurate paraphrase, as it implies that stress is a universal experience that individuals face in their daily lives.
questions.common_mistake: Many students mistake 'experientially' for 'experimentally' (which is actually a typo in the provided source passage). Even when reading the passage, students often choose Option A because it sounds logical, but 'experientially' refers to the act of living through something, not the academic process of understanding something through experiments.

questions.passage: There are many indicators with which to assess or measure corruption. One of them is the affluent living habit of the public official compared to his /her income. Corruption occurs when a public official expects to be induced to perform an act which that public official is ordinarily required to do by law Corruption can slow down development one of the most widely discussed consequences of corruption is the distortion of governmental expenditure. questions.common_mistake: Students often choose 'supply' because they associate water with the word supply, but 'amount' is the grammatically correct quantifier for precipitation in this specific linguistic context.

questions.common_mistake: Students often choose 'inevitable' because they associate drought with being unavoidable; however, the passage focuses on the *severity* of the impact, making 'disastrous' the contextually superior choice.

The contrast structure used in the text implies that while one approach is reactive (emergency), the other is proactive or long-term. 'Organized' is the most appropriate term here as it contrasts with the spontaneous nature of 'emergency' measures, implying a structured, premeditated, and systematic approach to disaster management.
questions.common_mistake: Students often choose 'urgent' because it relates to disaster management, but 'urgent' is a synonym for 'emergency' and would therefore be redundant or contradictory in this context. 'Routine' is also incorrect because drought management requires strategic planning rather than mere daily habit.

questions.explanation: The context of the passage describes the ripple effects of a drought. When people are forced to abandon their lands and suffer from famine, other negative consequences arise alongside (or at the same time as) these primary issues. The word 'parallel' in this context means occurring at the same time or being of a similar nature, referring to the secondary social and economic crises (like distress sales of cattle) that accompany the primary crisis of famine. While 'simultaneous' denotes timing, 'parallel' is a better stylistic choice in professional English to describe consequences that track alongside a main event.
questions.common_mistake: Students often choose 'simultaneous' (C) because it implies happening at the same time, but in this specific linguistic context, 'parallel' is frequently used to describe independent but related occurrences that run side-by-side with a major disaster.

'Action', 'process', and 'plan' are too generic and do not fit the formal tone of 'relief scheme' in this context.
questions.common_mistake: Students often choose 'plan' (Option D) because it seems synonymous with a strategy. However, in formal English used in policy and agriculture, a government initiative for distributing aid is specifically referred to as a 'scheme'.
